Physics: The section spans the BITSAT physics syllabus well (mechanics, heat, waves, optics, electricity, modern physics) with no duplicated concepts and clean, self-contained data in almost every item. The level is uniformly single-formula, 30–60 s work, which suits BITSAT, though Q13, Q18 and Q30 are close to pure recall and only Q12, Q16 and Q22 demand any multi-step handling. Fix the Q1 key (and its figure check) and tighten the Q10 wording before printing.

[major] The key inverts the wave relation: 0.2 Hz is the λ/v distractor (and 80 Hz is vλ), so for the graph's wavelength (4 m, giving the 5 Hz and 10 Hz distractors) the correct answer is B, f = v/λ = 5 Hz — recheck the figure and re-key.
[minor] A single excited hydrogen atom can emit at most 3 photons on cascading to the ground state, so the stem should read "a sample of hydrogen atoms excited to n = 4" to justify the answer 6.

Chemistry: All thirty keys check out and the spread across physical, inorganic and organic chapters is good, with no data gaps or figure contradictions in the computational items (q43, q50, q52, q60 are clean, quick calculations). The level, however, leans heavily on single-step factual recall (q34, q36, q38, q41, q47, q49, q54) and is a touch easy for BITSAT, with only two or three items demanding genuine multi-step reasoning. Tightening the electrochemistry pair and adding one or two more reasoning-based physical-chemistry items would improve discrimination.

[minor] The only difference between keys A and B is the vinyl vs cyclopentadienyl cation ranking, which requires antiaromatic destabilisation (outside the NCERT/BITSAT treatment of aromaticity); replace IV with a simple secondary/primary alkyl cation so the discrimination stays within syllabus.

[minor] This tests the same concentration-dependence of molar conductivity that the Kohlrausch calculation in q43 already covers; swap it for a different electrochemistry concept (e.g. Faraday's law, Nernst equation or conductance-cell geometry) to avoid intra-section overlap.
[minor] Hot alkaline KMnO4 gives the benzoate salt, so the stem should add "followed by acidification" for benzoic acid to be the strictly correct product.

English Proficiency: The section covers the expected spread — idiom, para jumble, synonym/antonym, error spotting, voice, sentence completion and a two-question comprehension set — and the RC passage is well written and appropriately sized for the time budget. However, the vocabulary items (legible, praised) sit well below BITSAT difficulty and two of them share the same sentence, so the lexical challenge should be raised and de-duplicated. Fix the mis-keyed synonym and the option labelling before printing; the grammar and reading items are otherwise sound.
[major] The key is wrong: CANDID means frank/open, so the answer is (A) Frank, not (C) Ornate.
[minor] Every option carries a duplicated label ("(A) (A) legible"), and the stem contains a literal "\n\n" instead of a line break, so the item needs clean typesetting.

[minor] This item recycles Q65's sentence (teacher praised the student for neat handwriting) and tests the very word "praised" already supplied there, and "praised/criticized" is too elementary for BITSAT — use a fresh, harder word.

Logical Reasoning: The section covers the standard BITSAT logical-reasoning spread (syllogism, series, coding, relations, ranking, spatial/figure items) with keys that check out wherever the data is complete, including the complementary-pair syllogism in Q71 and the n²−1 error term in Q90. Difficulty is appropriate for roughly 60–90 s per item, though Q79 and Q80 sit at the very easy end and could be replaced with slightly richer relation/classification items. The blocking issues are production-side: the two odd-figure-out items (Q75, Q81) carry no artwork at all, and several items have duplicated option text or labels that must be fixed before print.
[major] All four options are blank and no figure is supplied (no figure marker either), so the odd-figure-out item is unanswerable as printed.
[major] Like Q75, the four option figures are missing entirely, leaving no basis for the stated key B.
[minor] The code token 'Cl' in the second sentence breaks the single-capital-letter code pattern and should be a single letter (e.g. 'G'); the answer N is unaffected.
[minor] The option list (A) Mango … (D) Carrot is printed twice and the duplicate block must be deleted.
[minor] Option labels are doubled ('(A) (A) Facade'), the same rendering glitch seen in Q86, Q87 and Q90, and should be cleaned up before printing.

Mathematics: The section covers the syllabus broadly and evenly (calculus, algebra, coordinate geometry, vectors/3D, probability and statistics), and all keys I checked compute correctly, with most items solvable in well under 90 seconds. The main defects are the genuinely ambiguous direction-cosine options in qno 108 and the near-identical parabola pair 109/110, plus a mild overlap in the definite-integral property questions; a few items (92, 106, 118) are very easy one-step recall but acceptable as warm-up questions. Several stems (93, 96, 107, 108, 124, 126, 129) are written in plain ASCII rather than the LaTeX used elsewhere and should be typeset consistently before printing.

[major] Options (A) ±(3/13, −4/13, 12/13) and (B) (3/13, −4/13, 12/13) are both defensible sets of direction cosines for the given direction ratios, so the item has two correct answers and one option must be replaced.
[minor] The item is tagged "Limits and Continuity" but is a Conic Sections (parabola) question, so the topic label must be corrected.

[major] This duplicates qno 109 almost exactly (write the parabola from a given vertex and focus on an axis), so one of the pair should be replaced by a different conic concept such as eccentricity, directrix or a tangent condition.

[minor] This tests the same reflection trick (adding f(x) and f(a+b−x) to cancel the awkward factor) as qno 96, so consider swapping it for a definite-integral item using a different property or a substitution.
